title: Medical Translator vs. Interpreter Differences and AI Safety
summary: Learn the difference between medical translation and interpretation, including why AI medical translation and AI medical interpretation need different safety checks.
body_markdown:
###


A medical translator works with written text. A medical interpreter works with spoken or signed communication. The jobs use different skills, happen on different timelines, and need different quality checks.


###


Sight translation is an oral version of a written document. It can help with short written material during a live encounter, but it does not give the patient a translated document to keep.


###


Written translation can be reviewed before use, but errors can persist across a full document or repeated template. Live interpreting happens turn by turn, so safety checks need to catch omissions, changed meaning, numbers, medication terms, and speaker changes while the conversation is happening.


###


No. HHS guidance calls for qualified human translator review in certain written machine-translation cases, including when accuracy is required, the source is complex or technical, or the text affects rights, benefits, or meaningful access. The rule applies to text-based machine translation.


###


Yes. A healthcare AI system can support both live interpreting and written translation, but the same safety process should not be used for both. Spoken care needs live quality checks, while written materials need document-level checks.
